request.description:
Regression from watch's raw-mode keys. term.MakeRaw (watch_keys.go:283) disables ISIG, so Ctrl-C arrives as a key; watch.go:991-997 returns interrupted() → 1 (or ExitHeld) without cancelling the context. attachRun (run.go:618) and runCloudAttach (run_cloud.go:80) map 1→5 'detached' only when ctx.Err()!=nil, so a person who presses Ctrl-C or q on `ticfac run` gets exit 1 and 'the watch was interrupted' while the run keeps going: the misread tick 8v3 fixed. Tests mask it (run_test swaps attach for a context cancel; TestWatchOnATerminalTakesKeys asserts 1 for q on a live run). Fix: make a key interrupt indistinguishable from a cancel to attach callers (cancel or return the running class), and test the real attach with a key.
evidence: internal/cli/watch_keys.go:283; internal/cli/watch.go:991-997, :861-871; internal/cli/run.go:611-628; internal/cli/run_cloud.go:80

ticfac run epic-hn6 filed this backlog tick from the finding f4eb2fa44e734550e6ab79a430404933e475459be5940f9d3e3ebb5640180145 (reported by run-epic-hn6/tick-v16/attempt-1): the done is reachable with the finding standing, so it is a backlog tick with an owner rather than the epic's to absorb. The decision record is .ticfac/runs/epic-hn6/absorptions/f4eb2fa44e734550e6ab79a430404933e475459be5940f9d3e3ebb5640180145.json on the run branch.
request.title: Ctrl-C/q on a terminal under `ticfac run` exits 1, not 5 'detached'
